newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, seen flat before earnings data.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, seen flat before earnings data.

text.p: Polish shares eased in lower turnover on Wednesday and analysts saw them flat in the next two sessions, with the market awaiting companies' monthly earnings reports for September, most of them due on Friday.
The main market's WIG index eased 0.3 percent to 14,908.3 and turnover fell 11.3 percent to 108.8 million zlotys ($38.9 million) on both markets as 55 issues fell, 12 rose and 13 were flat.

"It's likely to be quiet as investors wait for the earnings reports, although it's surprising we don't have much of the usual speculative play ahead of the reports' release," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski of Bank Gdanski brokerage.
Some analysts said good earnings could send the market up to resistance at 15,200 or even 15,600 points of the main WIG index sometime over the next two weeks.
But others said the bourse, which has risen nearly 100 percent since the start of the year, was likely to experience a profit-taking correction and fall to 14,400 or 13,500 points.

Analysts said Bank Ochrony Srodowiska SA (BOS), which starts its public offering on Monday and seeks a main-market bourse listing in January, is likely to draw some capital from shares, which could hurt bourse prices.
Analysts said confectioner Wedel SA surged 9.9 percent in six-million-zloty ($2.1 million) trade on speculation the firm would report good September earnings.
Continuous trade turnover was at 2.4 million zlotys ($0.9 million) with top mover construction firm Budimex up 3.6 percent.
Mass privatisation NFI units fell 1.6 percent in 20.5-million-zloty ($7.3 million) trade in the regular bourse session but rose 3.3 percent in 17.7-million-zloty ($6.3 million) continuous trade.
